full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original Suit being Title Suit No. 01 of 1998 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Char Fashion, Bhola for declaration of title and further declaration that the order dated 30.12.1997 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.92 of 1995-96 described in schedule 'Kha' of the plaint is illegal, collusive and not bindirig upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia, that the suit land measuring 00810 'shahasrangsho' appertaining to plot no.4205/6 of Mouza Char Tofazzal described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint was a khash land under the government. The predecessor of the plaintiffs namely Abdul Mannan Mijhi prayed for settlement of the land from the government and the government being satisfied pursuant to a Group Settlement Case No. 157-17/50-51 granted a settlement for the 'Ga' schedule suit land situated within "Dularhat bazar" in favour of Abdul Mannan Mijhi. Thereafter; the settlement holder Abdul Mannan paid 'selami' to the government and the government accepted the same after granting D.C.R. The predecessor of the plaintiffs erected this shop in the suit land and was continuing his business therein. After the death of Abdul Mannan the plaintiffs inherited the suit property and possessing the same. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that their predecessor on 15.09.1954 and 13.03.1955 paid 'selami and obtained D.C.R. and for the last 50 (fifty) years the plaintiffs are possessing the suit shop. On 25.12.1992 the dacoits put fire to 'Dularhat Bazar in where the plaintiffs shop is situated. Subsequently, for a new khatian in the name of the plaintiffs they filed an application in the office of the defendant No.3 and accordingly a Miscellaneous Case being No.92/95-96 was started. The defendant No.3 asked the defendant No. 1 to inspect the matter and submit a report but the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 in collusion with the defendants No. 1 and 2 managed to submit a false report. The defendant Nos. 4 and 5 while tried to grab the property and the defendant No.3 by his order dated 30.12.1997 being bias in their favour started proceeding of a miscellaneous case to grant re-settlement, the plaintiffs instituted the original suit. 

 6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan Mijhi in respect of the suit land obtained settlement from the government rightly pursuant to a Group Settlement Case; which is in existence and have been called for but complying the direction of this court in civil revision No. 3800 of 2007 the concerned government official without sending the complete file sent the case record partially with an ill motive and the paper sent clearly go to show that the plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan in serial. No. 24 obtained settlement of the suit land followed by payment of salami in favour of the government by two D.C.R./Receipts. The learned Advocate also submits that the lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal consulting the said Group Settlement Case and the certified copy marked as Exhibit-I rightly held that, pursuant' to two D.C.R marked as Exhibit-2 and 2(Ka) the government accepted Abdul Mannan as settlement-holder under them. It is in fact proved by Exhibits I, 2 and 2(ka) that the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Abdul Mannan applied for settlement of the suit land which was subsequently allowed and thereafter salami was paid by the settlement holder Abdul Mannan. The learned appellate court clearly observed in his findings and decision that the claim of the plaintiffs appears to be correct in view of the exhibited papers but subsequently the Court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in holding the view that the settlement was not completed by opening a separate khatian in the name of plaintiffs predecessor. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below misconstrued the factual aspect of the case inasmuch as it is the specific assertion of the plaintiffs that for opening a separate khatian in their name while they submitted an application before the concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land) Char Fashion, a miscellaneous case was started. But the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 collusively managed to stop that proceeding only to deprive the plaintiffs and thereby the plaintiffs felt aggrieved and instituted the original suit. The learned Advocate argued that the findings of the lower appellate court itself is self-contradictory and as such perverse in the eye of law. In support of group settlement the learned Advocate referred a decision of this Court reported in 2 D.R. 265 passed in the case of 'The Province of Bengal vs. Nalini Kanto Baraijja Chowdhury and others. 

 9. On perusal of the case records it transpires that previously in respect of the disputed property there was another Civil Revision being No. 3800 of 2007 in this court invoking the provisions laid down in section 115(1) of, the Code of Civil Procedure and in that Civil Revision the Rule was made absolute with an order of remand to the appellate court for passing a fresh judgment after rectification and compliance of a direction. For proving the genuineness of the plaintiffs claim of settlement from the government and for proper adjudication into the matter of -controversy the group settlement case record was called for as per direction of this Court. After getting partial of that case record; the lower appellate court found the existence of the Group settlement case. Following the direction of this court on an application from the side of the plaintiffs the court of appeal called for the original record/volume from the offices of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion as well as A.D.C. (Rev.), Bhola.' It has come to the notice of this court that after getting the order of the Court partial original papers were sent without sending the case record as a whole and the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion, Bhola sent the Roll of K.M. settlement, wherefrom it is apparent that a Group Settlement Case No. 157-F/1950-51 was started and the page of said settlement-roll go to show that there are four settlement holders whose serial numbers are 23,24,25 and 26. In serial No. 24 there is an inclusion of plaintiffs predecessor's name viz. Abdul Mannan Mijhi, son of Arfan Ali Mijhi. Against the name of that Abdul Mannan it has been clearly mentioned that the disputed land of schedule cka' measuring an area of 00810 `Shahasrangsa' in plot No. 4205/6 under the government khash khatian has been settled by the government in the year 1-957 in favour of Abdul Mannan Mijhi and the amount of Salami was fixed against the suit land. It is to be noted here that the land included within this paper marked as Exhibit-1 and in respect of the land of the government khash khatian 04(four) persons having serial No. 23-26 obtained settlement pursuant to a K.M. settlement roll and therefore it is clear that the said settlement of the government is nothing but a group settlement as contended by the plaintiffs. Apart from this; it is obvious to note that the concerned tahshilder pursuant to that settlement granted receipts in favour of the' plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan after acceptance of selami against the disputed property. In the year 1998 also the concerned official after acceptance of rent granted receipts in favour of plaintiffs predecessor-in-interest vide Exhibits No.2 and 2(ka). 

 10. In this context; having gone through the impugned judgment and decree I find that the learned appellate court below scanning the said papers conclusively held that on perusal of the certified copy of K.M. settlement case marked as exhibit- l along with two D.C.Rs. it appears that the plaintiffs predecessor Abdul Mannan in Group Settlement Case No.157-F/1950-51 in serial No.24 obtained the suit land and accordingly paid selami in favour of the government. It is also held by the lower appellate court that the claim of the plaintiffs appears to be correct. Subsequent to that; the learned court below holding the view that inasmuch as the settlement was not completed and no khatian was opened neither in the name of the settlement holder nor in the names of the plaintiffs; the plaintiffs are not entitled to get the relief as prayed for. It is the observation of the appellate court in the concluding portion of the impugned judgment that:বাদী পক্ষের পূববর্তী আঃ মান্নানের নামে নাঃ ভূমি বাবদ  ১৫৭/৫০-৫১ নং গ্রুপ সেটেলমেন্ট কেস রজু থাকায় উযধশক্ত বন্দোবস্তের বিষয়টি চুড়ান্ত করার নিমিত্তে আবশ্যকীয় প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা যুক্তে বাদী পক্ষের আদালতের স্নরনাপন্ন হওয়া যুক্তিযুক্ত ও সংগত ছিল। From the aforesaid recital of the impugned judgment and decree it is evident that the lower appellate court awarded no decree in favour of the plaintiffs inasmuch as the appropriate relief was not sought for. 

 12. I have come across from the relevant papers that the suit land is situated within a bazar area commonly known as 'Dularhat' and it is not denied from any corner that in the year 1992 'Dularhat Bazar' was burnt into ashes. It is the pleading's case of the plaintiffs that after the demise of their father they possess the suit shop and subsequently for opening a khatian in their names they filed an application and went to the defendant No.3, A.D.C.(Rev.), Bhola. In the office of the A.D.C. (Rev.) admittedly a Misc. case was started for opening a khatian in the names of the plaintiffs in respect of the disputed property but before disposal of that Miscellaneous case it was filed (" "). It is also within records that the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 tried to obtain a new khatian in their names from the office of the defendant No.3 A.D.C. (Rev.). Challenging the said act of the defendants the plaintiffs instituted the original suit.
